open_questions: STATE MACHINE (units_held) IMPLEMENTATION — flag for reviewer per the card's explicit ask: units_held in {0,1,2,3} is a single-magic internal counter persisted via GlobalVariableSet/Get keyed 'QM_9644_<symbol>_{units_held,unit1_entry_price,unit1_atr,unit1_entry_time,unit1_cat_stop,bars_since_unit1}'. NO multiple magic numbers are used (card forbids it). The 3-unit cap is STRUCTURAL (three fixed ladder rungs, no path beyond unit-3) and deliberately NOT an input, so it cannot be tuned past 3. One unit is added per closed D1 bar; units_held advances only on a CONFIRMED fill (OnUnitFilled). On OnInit and again on the first tick the persisted state is reconciled against live positions (units_held>0 with zero live positions for this magic -> ResetState), which self-heals a stale GlobalVariable left by a prior tester run in the shared GV pool.

AGGREGATE CATASTROPHIC STOP DESIGN — flag for reviewer: the stop is a SINGLE fixed level cat_stop = unit1_entry_price - strategy_catastrophic_atr(4.0)*unit1_atr, snapshotted at unit-1 entry and held fixed (NOT re-snapshotted per unit, per card). It is enforced two ways at the IDENTICAL price: (a) every leg is opened with req.sl = cat_stop -- because the level is the same for all legs and never changes there is no per-leg OrderModify race; (b) an authoritative per-tick VIRTUAL stop in Strategy_ManageOpenPosition closes ALL legs atomically (QM_EXIT_SL_HIT) the moment Bid <= cat_stop, rather than relying on the tester filling three separate broker SLs. Both fire at the same level so they are always consistent. Reviewer: confirm you accept the belt-and-suspenders (broker SL + virtual stop) at one shared level over a virtual-stop-only design.

PER-UNIT 1/3 SIZING — flag for reviewer: each unit is opened via the explicit-risk overload QM_TM_OpenPosition(req, ticket, magic, RISK_MODE, budget/3) with req.sl = the SHARED cat_stop. RISK_FIXED stays 1000 (the TOTAL budget, satisfies HR4) and PORTFOLIO_WEIGHT stays 1.0 (left for Q11) -- the 1/3 split is NOT encoded in PORTFOLIO_WEIGHT. Because each of the 3 legs risks 1/3 of the budget measured to the same aggregate stop, the legs sum to the full budget at the stop -> bounded worst-case ~= budget. Note: additions are sized to each add's OWN entry-to-shared-stop distance (the card's 'scaled per-unit'), which is what makes the 3-leg worst-case sum to exactly the budget rather than exceed it.

CHAOS FILTER vs NEWS FILTER SCOPE — card ambiguity resolved by most-literal reading: the news filter is explicitly unit-1-only ('Unit-2/3 entries during news windows are allowed -- the trade is already on'), implemented by computing QM_NewsAllowsTrade2 once per tick and applying it inside Strategy_EntrySignal to g_pending_unit==1 ONLY. The vol-percentile chaos filter is worded generically ('skip new entries ...') WITHOUT the unit-1 qualifier, so it is applied to ALL new units (unit-1/2/3) via the central Strategy_NoTradeFilter return. If the reviewer intends the chaos filter to also carve out unit-2/3 (same 'trade already on' rationale as news), it is a one-line move into EntrySignal.

EXIT TIMING (TP) INTERPRETATION: card says 'exit everything at next bar's close after z>=0'. Realised as: detect z(shift1)>=0 on the just-closed D1 bar in AdvanceDaily, then flatten at the next session open (first tick of the new D1 bar) -- which equals the signal bar's CLOSE on gapless .DWX index CFDs (open[0]==close[1]). Symmetric with the entry convention ('enter at next session open'). A strict extra +1-bar delay is a one-line latch change if preferred.

TIME EXIT vs STALE-LADDER GATE: strategy_time_exit_days=10 flattens the whole ladder at 10 trading days from unit-1, while the 'skip unit-N if >15 days since unit-1' stale gate (strategy_stale_ladder_days=15) only bites at 15 days. With the default 10<15 the whole position is already closed before the 15-day gate can bind, so the stale gate is effectively subsumed by the time exit at defaults; it is still implemented literally per the card and becomes active only if P3 sweeps time_exit_days above stale_ladder_days.
